chunks: Abān narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who sold food for dirhams. When that term became due, he demanded payment from him, so he said: “I do not have dirhams; take food from me.”
He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it. He is only entitled to dirhams, and with them he may take whatever he wishes.”

key_terms.الْأَجَلُ: the specified term or due date for payment
key_terms.بِدَرَاهِمَ: for dirhams, indicating the original monetary price
key_terms.طَعَامًا: food commodity being sold or taken in settlement
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is legally unobjectionable
key_terms.يَأْخُذُ بِهَا مَا شَاءَ: he may take with it whatever he wishes, meaning he may receive equivalent settlement

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to accept goods instead of dirhams when a debt payment becomes due?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about settling a debt originally denominated in dirhams through goods when payment becomes due. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that there is no problem in accepting food instead, since the creditor is entitled to the value of the dirhams and may take what he wishes in exchange.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3944 - Aban narrated from Ya'qub bin Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (as) about a man who sold food for dirhams.
When the payment became due, he demanded his money, but the buyer said: "I do not have dirhams; take food instead."
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that. He is entitled to dirhams, and he may take whatever he wishes in exchange for them."
